text: Every child has a spark, but not every child gets the chance to show it. This is GranthAI. In Sanskrit, granth means a book, and its root means to tie together. We tie learning, people and opportunity together, around every child.

Across the world, talented children fall behind, not for lack of ability, but for lack of support. In Ireland, only fifty-four percent of children in care complete the Leaving Cert. And one teacher cannot sit beside twenty-five children every evening.
It starts with a profile. Aoife is nine. She picks what she loves: football, space and drawing. From her first answers, a Bayesian model starts tracking what she knows, and what to review next.

Here's the difference. Aoife asks a general chatbot: what's three quarters plus a half? It hands her the answer, and she copies it. GranthAI asks her to try first. When she answers four sixths, it spots the exact mistake, draws the pieces, and lets her find five quarters herself.

It works for every kind of question. Ask it to write your science homework, and it opens your teacher's class notes and a diagram of a leaf, then asks what the plant needs from the sun. Ask it to help you revise, and it builds a quick quiz on your weakest topics, and suggests a book you'll love. It never hands out answers. It helps children reach them.
Her feed follows her interests, to keep her curious. Gentle check-ins let her share how she feels, and if something is wrong, GranthAI never keeps secrets. It connects her with a trusted adult.

Now picture four schools. Each child is a node. Our ranking algorithms link children who share the same passions, across school walls, and the network settles into clusters: a space club, a coding crew, an art studio. Aoife joins pupils from two other schools to build a project together.
Each club is matched with a vetted retired teacher as a mentor, by subject, language and time. Children gain role models, and retired teachers gain meaningful work.

Teachers get their time back. GranthAI shows which topics the class understands and where they struggle, then helps plan the lesson: objectives, a hands-on activity, and a quick check, built from the curriculum and the teacher's own materials.
Future Me turns interests into real routes, from college courses to apprenticeships.
And it's safe by design: no ads, no selling data, no emotion detection, built for GDPR and the EU AI Act.

We are starting in Ireland's DEIS schools. Next, the UK. Then Europe, where millions of children learn in a second language. And one day, every community where one tablet serves a whole class. GranthAI. Not another chatbot, but a whole team around every child.
